paragraphs: With the iPhone’s 20th anniversary coming next year, Apple is reportedly experimenting with a range of designs, some of them ambitious revamps of the classic look. And some familiar features might go away, including the Dynamic Island.
Apple’s goal for the iPhone 20 seems to be to repeat what it did with the iPhone X in 2017: Lay the groundwork for what iPhone will look like for the next decade.

Apple likes to celebrate big anniversaries with significant redesigns. There’s no better example than the iPhone X. Back in 2017, this model eliminated the Home button to make room for a nearly edge-to-edge OLED display. Apple also introduced Face ID along with the screen notch. Virtually every iPhone since has followed this pattern.
The iPhone 20 is apparently set to do it again. Don’t expect it to be simply the current model with a faster processor. Not even close.

That said, this device remains nearly a year away. No industry leak can reveal exactly what it will look like because, at this point, Apple itself reportedly doesn’t know. Still, some of the company’s goals for the device have leaked out, along with descriptions of some prototypes. And time is running short — moving a device from prototype to assembly takes many months.

Apple is experimenting with four different designs for its 20th-anniversary iPhone, according to a new report from a noted tipster who goes by Ice Universe on Weibo. Two of the prototypes reportedly use conventional flat cover glass, while the other two feature quad-curved glass in which the screen’s glass gently bends downward along all four edges.

The two versions with curved glass could make the display appear almost bezel-free. They’ll actually have bezels measuring approximately 1 mm, according to the leaker, but the glass would curve gently toward the edges of the handset, helping conceal the borders when viewed straight on.

Ice Universe says these designs are the result of experiments with quad-curved glass over roughly three years. Apple has reportedly refined the design, reducing the curvature from more aggressive early prototypes. Work toward the final design continues.
